answer: Each identity must post a refundable bond per epoch and sign a rotating beacon seeded from the previous block hash, so ordering is unpredictable and one proof cannot be replayed across clones. A sybil farm must fund a separate bond per key and keep it locked through the vesting window, so cost scales linearly with identity count rather than being a one-off fee. Uptime slashes burn part of each bond, so a vine of idle clones bleeds money. An attacker pays far more than an honest agent with one pearl-sized stake.
